extracted.intended_audience: regulated facilities, state/tribal UIC permitting authorities, EPA staff, and public commenters on EPA CCS/Class VI rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: EPA Class VI CCS rule comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal/regulatory criteria relevant to Class VI Underground Injection Control permitting for geologic sequestration of CO2 and to the EPA's BSER/cost and technology determinations for CCS in rulemaking. Useful for drafting regulatory comments, compliance plans, or permit applications related to Class VI wells and CCS deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of review delineation (40 CFR 146.84(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 40 CFR 146.84(a), the area of review is the region surrounding the geologic sequestration project where USDWs may be endangered by the injection activity. The area of review is delineated using computational modeling that accounts for the physical and chemical properties of all phases of the injected carbon dioxide stream and is based on available site characterization, monitoring, and operational data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must use computational modeling that considers all phases of the injected CO2 stream and rely on available site characterization, monitoring, and operational data to delineate the area where USDWs could be endangered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective action for existing wells in the area of review
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC permitting authorities may require corrective action for existing wells within the area of review to ensure protection of underground sources of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting authorities can mandate remediation or corrective measures for wells identified by the area-of-review analysis to protect USDWs; applicants should anticipate and plan for potential corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seismic history submission requirement (40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: 40 CFR 146.82(a)(3)(v) requires the permit applicant to submit and the permitting authority to consider information on the seismic history including the presence and depth of seismic sources and a determination that the seismicity would not interfere with containment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit applications must include seismic-history data, identification and depths of seismic sources, and an analysis/determination that local seismicity will not compromise CO2 containment. See EPA implementation manual and references on induced seismicity (NRC 2013; GWPC/IOGCC 2021; EPA 2015 practical approaches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'confining zone' (40 CFR 146.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Confining zone” means a geological formation, group of formations, or part of a formation that is capable of limiting fluid movement above an injection zone. (40 CFR 146.3)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification of appropriate confining zones is required to demonstrate vertical containment; geological characterization must show the formation(s) can limit upward fluid movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency and Remedial Response Plan requirement (40 CFR 146.94(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: See EPA Emergency and Remedial Response Plan: 40 CFR 146.94(a) template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should prepare an Emergency and Remedial Response (ERR) Plan using the EPA template and the Class VI implementation manual guidance; the ERR plan must address emergency response and remedial measures to protect USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of underground sources of drinking water (USDWs) as a UIC Class VI standard
rubrics_metrics.description: UIC regulations for Class VI wells authorize the injection of CO2 for geologic sequestration while protecting human health by ensuring the protection of underground sources of drinking water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All permit conditions, area-of-review analyses, well construction, operation, monitoring, and corrective action plans must demonstrate protection of USDWs as the primary objective of Class VI permitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental justice considerations for Class VI permitting and primacy
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA (2023) Environmental justice Guidance for UIC Class VI Permitting and Primacy; EPA letters and memos incorporate EJ considerations into Class VI permitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting and primacy decisions should incorporate the EPA's EJ guidance; applicants and permitting authorities must consider EJ impacts, outreach, and mitigation when evaluating projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: UIC Class VI permit components (major components to protect USDWs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The major components to be included in UIC Class VI permits are detailed further in section VII.C.1.a.i(D)(4). (Preamble cross-reference)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the preamble cross-references detailed permit components, practitioners should ensure permits include area-of-review analyses, well construction and operation requirements, monitoring, emergency and remedial plans, corrective action provisions, and other elements designed to protect USDWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibitions and construction/operation requirements under UIC (40 CFR parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: See 40 CFR 144.12(b) (prohibition of movement of fluid into USDWs); 40 CFR 146.86(a)(1) (Class VI injection well construction requirements); 40 CFR 146 (Class VI operation requirements); 40 CFR 146.94 (emergency and remedial response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and permitting authorities must comply with the cited UIC regulatory provisions governing prohibition of contamination, well construction standards, operational requirements, and ERR obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA BSER determination factors (including cost)
rubrics_metrics.description: The EPA determines the BSER based on considering information on the statutory factors, including cost, on a source category or subcategory basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BSER analysis should evaluate statutory factors (e.g., cost, energy, feasibility) at the category/subcategory level; commenters can and should focus on cost evidence and category-level considerations in BSER debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: State flexibility via RULOF when source-specific costs differ
rubrics_metrics.description: If such a fundamental difference makes it unreasonable for a particular source to achieve the degree of emission limitation associated with implementing CCS with 90 percent capture, a state may provide a less stringent standard of performance (and/or longer compliance schedule, if applicable) for that source pursuant to the RULOF provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may adopt source-specific less-stringent standards or longer compliance schedules under RULOF where source-specific cost realities make the presumptive BSER impracticable; commenters should document any claimed fundamental cost differences to support such relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible extrapolation and technological forecasting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may extrapolate based on its findings and project technological improvements in a variety of ways: (1) extrapolate from testing results to predict a lower emissions rate than regularly achieved in testing (Essex Chem. Corp. v. Ruckelshaus); (2) forecast technological improvements allowing a lower emissions rate or effective control at larger plants than previously tested, provided the agency has adequate knowledge (Sierra Club v. Costle); (3) extrapolate based on testing at a particular kind of source to conclude that the technology will also be effective at a different, related, source (Lignite Energy Council v. EPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting future performance or broader applicability of a control technology, the agency must have adequate knowledge/support; commenters challenging extrapolation should address the adequacy of the evidentiary basis and assumptions behind forecasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequately demonstrated vs. achievable legal standard
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is the system which must be adequately demonstrated and the standard which must be achievable.” (Essex Chem. Corp. v. Ruckelshaus, 486 F.2d 427, 433 (1973)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory findings must show the control system is adequately demonstrated and that the emission standard it supports is achievable in practice; evidence should address both system demonstration and achievability at the regulated scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using EPAct05-assisted projects as demonstration evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: EPAct05 provisions (e.g., 42 U.S.C. 15962(a) and IRC section 48A(g)) provide that no technology or level of emission reduction shall be considered adequately demonstrated for purposes of CAA section 111 solely by reason of use at facilities receiving assistance under EPAct05 or by facilities receiving tax credits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence of technology performance drawn solely from projects supported by EPAct05 assistance or tax credits cannot by itself establish that a technology is 'adequately demonstrated' for BSER purposes; commenters relying on such projects should provide additional, independent demonstration data or address the statutory limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost analysis inputs and amortization assumptions (use of tax-credit periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 12-year amortization period is consistent with the period of time during which the IRC section 45Q tax credit can be claimed. (The EPA also references 7-year amortization assumptions in other analyses where appropriate.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost and economic analyses should state and justify amortization periods and other financial assumptions (e.g., tax-credit applicability) used to estimate CCS costs; use of consistent and justified amortization assumptions affects per-MWh and $/ton estimates and BSER cost considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of NETL/DOE cost and performance baselines and TSD for technical/cost detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed cost information, assessment of technology options, and demonstration of cost reasonableness can be found in the final TSD, GHG Mitigation Measures for Steam Generating Units. EPA used NETL Baseline Report costs directly for certain BSER analyses and adjusted reported costs to reflect 2022 dollars where noted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of CCS costs and feasibility should reference and, where appropriate, justify use of NETL/DOE baselines, cost models (e.g., FE/NETL CO2 Saline Storage Cost Model), and the EPA technical support documents (TSDs); commenters should explain if and why alternative cost inputs are preferable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment and management of injection-induced seismicity
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA and other bodies (NRC 2013; GWPC/IOGCC 2021; EPA 2015) provide guidance on induced seismicity potential and practical approaches to minimizing and managing potential impacts of injection-induced seismicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit applications and rulemaking analyses should assess induced seismicity potential, propose monitoring and mitigation measures, and reference relevant technical/regulatory guidance; seismic risk is an explicit part of the permit evaluation (see seismic-history submission requirement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative timelines and workforce/resource evaluation assumptions for CCS deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: The representative timeline for CCS assumes approximately a 3-year period for construction activities across capture, pipeline, and sequestration components, with pre-construction and permitting assumptions noted; evaluating workforce and resource requirements over a five-year period is reasonable. EPA is finalizing a limited one-year compliance date extension mechanism for certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses of feasibility, workforce needs, and compliance scheduling should document timeline assumptions (construction, permitting, start dates), justify evaluation periods (e.g., five-year resource assessment), and consider available regulatory mechanisms for limited extensions.
